[00:00] Jordan: All right, thanks everybody for jumping on. quick intros — im Jordan, AE on the account, with Priya from our se team. how's everyone doing?
[00:18] Marta: Good, thanks. excited to get clarity on the performance side — we need latency guarantees for our customer-facing chat flows.
[00:28] Ryan: hi, quick note i might drop in and out, i'm juggling the release window but I'll stay for the core.
[00:34] Priya: great, goal for today is to pick concrete TTFT vs TPOT targets, agree sampling and measurement, and set dates for the smoke-run. we'll propose a measurement rig that maps to your traffic.
[01:05] Deepak: To start, our primary workload is conversational support triage. average prompt length 120 tokens, responses ~200 tokens. bursty evening traffic, 30rps sustained during peak windows, spikes to 120rps for short periods.
[01:33] Priya: ok, that's useful. question on tail sensitivity — do you care more about first-token latency for the agent handoff, or overall total time for the user-visible response?
[01:48] Marta: both matter, but user experience conversations say first token matters for perceived snappiness, while overall time affects downstream metrics like abandonment. so we want a hybrid SLO: TTFT p95 300ms, TTFT p99 550ms, TPOT p95 1.4s, TPOT p99 2.2s as starting hypothesis.
[02:14] Jordan: those are reasonable starting points. one thing to call out — our measurement lab differentiates between cold key-value misses and warm KV hits; if you have many multi-turn sessions we get warm-cache benefits. are those numbers measured with warm state?
[02:33] Deepak: they are from our current provider with no session cache, so warm-cache would be a win for us. we should plan tests for both warm and cold scenarios.
[02:44] Priya: agreed — for the pilot, we recommend three buckets: cold-starts, warm session steady-state, and long-tail large context (>1024 tokens). we'll instrument KV prefix cache vs no-cache runs.
[03:05] Evelyn: on compliance, any retention from sandbox runs? we need to make sure logs and transcripts in the trial are ephemeral or routed to our S3 with encryption.
[03:20] Jordan: yes we can toggle retention and we will use customer-controlled KMS for the private pilot. we'll include retention settings in the runbook.
[03:33] Ryan: back to SLOs — what's your recommended sample size for p99 to be statistically meaningful? we've seen vendors quote p99 on small sample sets.
[03:46] Priya: excellent question. for p99 we recommend at least 30k measurements per target scenario, but practically for the pilot we do stratified sampling: run a 4-hour sustained load with synthetic traffic that reproduces your spike profile to collect ~50k samples. plus separate burst tests to capture spikes.
[04:12] Marta: 50k sounds heavy but acceptable if it gives confidence. timeline wise how long to setup?
[04:19] Jordan: we can provision a Dedicated staging pool in 24-48 hours after we get VPC details. smoke-run (2 hour) + 4-hour sustained run + 2 short burst tests would take a day to execute, then 48 hours to analyze. so propose week of 11/16 for execution.
[04:41] Deepak: on the run configuration — are you going to use Redwood's continuous-batching defaults? we may want to tune batching to prioritize latency at low rps.
[04:55] Priya: yes by default we have continuous batching with an adaptive window. for the measurement we lock the batching and also run a low-latency mode with smaller batch sizes to show tradeoffs. we'll provide config diff.
[05:12] Jordan: also planning to test quantized model variants for cost tradeoffs. we'll show delta on TPOT and per-1M token cost.
[05:24] Ryan: do you include network RTT inside TTFT? our internal definition excludes client->edge RTT; we want server-side only.
[05:34] Priya: we'll capture both: end-to-end from client (your synthetic agent) and server-only (server ingress to first token emitted). we'll be explicit in the runbook which metric is which.
[05:49] Marta: what about p95 vs p99 thresholds? we may accept slightly higher p99 for infrequent long contexts but p95 should be tight.
[05:58] Priya: that's why we propose a weighted acceptance: p95 must meet target for 95% of traffic; p99 allowed slack up to +20% on initial pilot but we'll define escalation if regressions occur.
[06:15] Jordan: quick note on fallback policies — if a heavy prompt triggers a long inference time we'll fall back to a smaller model variant as part of the trial to avoid user-visible outages. we can demonstrate continuity.
[06:28] Deepak: good. curious about the measurement tooling — are you instrumenting per-token traces and traces exported to Jaeger/OTEL?
[06:37] Priya: we emit OTEL spans with first-token, generation-done timestamps, kernel-level exit points, and batching boundaries. we'll share a sample dashboard. some names in the exported spans may be slightly off in auto transcript (like kv-cache -> "K V cache"), but it's fine for trace correlation.
[07:02] Marta: excellent. can you model cost per QPS for the different quant/Batching combinations?
[07:09] Jordan: yes, cost model will be included in the deliverable spreadsheet. we'll present TPOT vs cost delta and show recommended operating point.
[07:20] Ryan: anything we should provide beyond traffic sample and VPC details?
[07:25] Priya: a short prompt corpus capturing your 90th and 99th percentile long-turns and a list of top 50 intents helps for quality regression checks.
[07:36] Marta: we'll extract those from production logs and scrub PII, Evelyn will sign off.
[07:41] Evelyn: yes, we'll share a redacted dataset. retention and access controls documented please.
[07:48] Jordan: noted. on measurement specifics, summary recommendation for pilot acceptance: TTFT p95 <= 300ms, TTFT p99 <= 600ms, TPOT p95 <= 1.5s, TPOT p99 <= 2.5s for warm-state; allow cold-state to exceed by up to 1.5x but must be measured separately. sound ok?
[08:09] Marta: that's in line with expectations, as long as we have visibility into warm/cold splits.
[08:15] Priya: we'll include a sampling plan:
- 4-hour sustained test matching your diurnal peak (aim 30rps sustained),
- 3x 10-minute spike tests to 120rps spaced across the run,
- 1-hour warm-state session emulation with session affinity,
- separate cold-start sweep over long-context (>1k tokens) prompts.
[08:47] Jordan: measurement outputs: raw latency logs, OTEL traces, per-request model variant, batch-size histogram, token counts, and cost-per-1k tokens. we'll deliver processed SLO tables with p50/p95/p99 and confidence intervals.
[09:02] Ryan: for p99 confidence intervals, will you annotate how many samples are in each bucket? critical for legal/compliance.
[09:08] Priya: yes — every p99 will report sample count and 95% bootstrap CI.
[09:14] Deepak: what about production handoff after pilot? do you support A/B rollouts and canary config?
[09:20] Jordan: absolutely — Redwood Dedicated supports canary routing and automatic fallback to hosted variants. we'll outline a ramp plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 2 weeks with guardrails.
[09:34] Marta: good. any red flags on our side? we have a shared infra firewall that drops long-lived websocket streams, would that affect streaming TTFT measurements?
[09:45] Priya: we'd run both streaming and non-streaming measurement; for TTFT streaming we measure first partial token arrival — if your firewall breaks long streams we can emulate chunked responses over HTTP to replicate the UX.
[09:58] Jordan: okay practical next steps recap — Jordan to send harness + pricing + runbook; Priya to attach recommended configs and dashboard sample; Deepak to share network/VPC info; Halcyon to provide traffic sample and intent corpus. target smoke-run week of 11/16, analysis by EOD 11/18, follow up on 11/19 to review results.
[10:27] Marta: that timeline works.
[10:33] Jordan: any further Qs?
[10:36] Ryan: none from me.
[10:38] Evelyn: please include data retention toggles in the runbook — we need auto-delete after 7 days.
[10:45] Priya: noted, we'll add a retention flag.
[10:49] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll send the artifacts. meeting adjourned.
